title: Cross-Ministry Collaboration to Tackle Problematic Gaming amongst Youths
what_it_is: Cross-Ministry Collaboration to Tackle Problematic Gaming amongst Youths

sections.label: MOE student mental well-being support
sections.summary: MOE works with other Government agencies to support students' mental well-being and healthy digital media engagement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) works closely with other Government agencies to support students' mental well-being and healthy engagement with digital media.

sections.label: Gaming concerns referral and parenting resources
sections.summary: Schools refer students with gaming concerns to social service agencies or NAMS, and MOE co-developed parenting and technology use resources.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Schools identify students with gaming concerns and refer them, with parental consent where required, to social service agencies (SSAs) for early intervention or to the National Addiction Management Service (NAMS) under the Institute of Mental Health for assessment and treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: MOE has partnered the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Health Promotion Board to develop the Parenting for Wellness resources to equip parents with parenting knowledge and strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In addition, the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, MOE and MSF co-developed the "Positive Use Guide on Technology and Social Media", which includes practical tips on limiting gaming activities.

sections.label: Online safety regulatory measures
sections.summary: The Government introduced measures including the 2022 Broadcasting Act, the Code of Practice for Online Safety, and 2025 app distribution services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: In terms of the regulatory aspects of managing the online space, the Government has progressively introduced measures to better protect users, in particular, children when they go online over the years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: We have made some of the regulatory changes, in particular in 2022, with the Broadcasting Act, the introduction of the Code of Practice for Online Safety that was promulgated by the Infocomm Media Development Authority for social media services, and later in 2025, also with app distribution services.

sections.label: Gaming platform engagement and regulatory levers
sections.summary: The Ministry does not currently engage gaming platforms directly, but has regulatory levers through the Broadcasting Act and Code of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: In terms of the engagement with the gaming platforms, we do not, at least currently, engage them directly as a Ministry in terms of how they promulgate the nature of gaming to make it less addictive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: I think it is within the remit of the gaming platforms to decide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: But we do have regulatory levers at this point of time through the Broadcasting Act, as well as the Code of Practice for Online Safety, as mentioned earlier.
